description: Daily active users: the number of distinct users in a day, the usual starting point of an estimate.
Queries (requests) per second; on average, requests per day divided by 86,400 seconds.
Peak traffic divided by average traffic; systems are sized for the peak, often 2 to 3 times the average when nothing is measured.
How many requests read compared with how many write; writes must reach primary storage, reads can be served by caches and replicas.
How many copies of each byte are stored; it multiplies the raw storage estimate.
2^10 ≈ a thousand (KB), 2^20 ≈ a million (MB), 2^30 ≈ a billion (GB), 2^40 ≈ a trillion (TB), 2^50 ≈ a quadrillion (PB).
Memory reference ~100 ns, SSD random read ~tens to 100 µs, data center round trip ~0.5 ms, cross-continent round trip ~150 ms.
